A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the radiation response of CMOS devices is not simply a matter of the junction photocurrent.
the transient response of a CMOS integrated circuit is a complicated function of the circuit design, the circuit operating voltage, and the radiation dose-rate.
the radiation response of a CMOS device is determined by two effects: the net photocurrent and the parasitic four layer structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CMOS circuits are very sensitive to high dose rates of ionizing radiation.
the radiation response of CMOS circuits can be quite different from that of bipolar circuits.
CMOS circuits can be designed to withstand high dose rates without suffering latch-up or permanent damage.
